A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same MoLAR research, despite v5's changed title. Their main text, equations, figures, tables, and Appendices A-D are readable and support a reliable comparison.

before.justification: V4 reports original OOD detection and semi-supervised classification results, component ablations, and initialization analyses in Tables 1-6 and Appendices B-C.

after.justification: V5 retains original experiments and adds ImageNet-200 OOD detection and classification results, plus CIFAR-100 component ablations.

M1.justification: The MoLAR/MoLAR-SS procedures, SKMPS selection, vMF-SNE initialization, and Algorithms 1-3 are retained. The corrected loss formulas align with v4's already stated cross-entropy training and do not establish a different training procedure.

E1.justification: V5 substantially expands OOD coverage beyond CIFAR-10/100 as ID datasets by adding ImageNet-200 with SSB-hard, NINCO, iNaturalist, OpenImage-O, and DTD evaluations. It also adds ImageNet-200 semi-supervised classification in Table 5. Existing dataset coverage is retained.

E2.justification: Table 1 drops DeepEnsemble, KNN, LogitNorm, and PixMix, substantially narrowing its ResNet comparison to CIDER and PALM. The RoPAWS/RoPAWS-VM comparison in v4 Table S14 also disappears. The principal frozen-backbone comparators remain unchanged.

E3.justification: The added ImageNet-200 evaluations specify 600 SKMPS exemplars, corresponding to three per class, and compare exemplar-based with full-training-set KNN detection. Table 6 adds component-control settings for CIFAR-100. Existing splits, metrics, backbone configurations, and training budgets are retained.

E4.justification: Table 6 extends the vMF-SNE initialization and SKMPS ablation to CIFAR-100. Conversely, v4's RoPAWS compatibility experiment and associated discussion are removed. The training-curve, exemplar-diversity, initialization-transfer, and hyperparameter analyses remain.

E5.justification: V4 states five-run mean and standard-deviation reporting for semi-supervised accuracy. V5 retains this practice for existing datasets but explicitly excludes ImageNet-200, whose Table 5 entries lack uncertainty estimates. No increase in repeated runs is established.

E6.justification: V5 adds ImageNet-200 results and CIFAR-100 ablation entries, removes RoPAWS results, and revises supervised CIFAR scores. For example, Table 1's MoLAR CIFAR-10 near/far AUROC changes from 96.8/98.2 to 95.4/99.1 under the retained reported setting, reversing its near-OOD ranking against the unchanged 95.8 backbone score. V5 also newly reports 5-times and 30-times inference speedups.

T1.justification: Equation 6 changes from an average class probability to negative mean log probability, correcting its claimed equivalence to cross-entropy. V5 also corrects the missing minus sign in the cross-entropy definition accompanying Equation 7. The remaining mathematical development is retained.

C1.justification: The abstract and contribution list strengthen the efficiency claim with up to 30-times faster OOD inference and foreground efficient foundation-model use. The central claims about unified supervised/semi-supervised detection and competitive classification remain.

C2.justification: Section 3 adds mechanism explanations concerning exemplar initialization, augmentation consistency, and automatic center updates through backpropagation. Section 4.2 qualifies the previously universal near-OOD advantage over the backbone with a CIFAR-10 exception and restricts the CIFAR-100 exemplar improvement to near-OOD detection.

D1.justification: V5 documents the new ImageNet-200 exemplar budget and full-dataset versus 600-exemplar evaluation configuration. Appendix D's implementation framework, training durations, hardware, and other technical details are retained. The printed code address points to the same repository linked in v4.

R1.justification: V5 adds five references covering Vision Transformers and the added OOD datasets. It more explicitly positions MoLAR as PAWS-inspired and foregrounds supervised representational OOD detection, while removing the related-work statement that no previous semi-supervised OOD method was known. The broader literature coverage remains similar.

P1.justification: The title, abstract, and introduction are substantially revised around efficient foundation-model OOD detection. Section 3 replaces the motivation and distributes the former combined comparison paragraph into component-specific related-method passages. Results, discussion, and portions of the appendix narrative are also reorganized or rewritten.

P2.justification: Figure 1 is redrawn to include ImageNet-200. V4 Figure 6 moves to Figure S10, while v5 Figure 6 redisplays part of the existing Figure S9 analysis. Tables 1, 2, 5, and 6 gain columns, and a new ImageNet-200 Table S13 is added. The basic layout and most existing figures remain.

improvement.justification: ImageNet-200 evaluations and CIFAR-100 ablations broaden empirical support, while corrected cross-entropy formulas and the explicit CIFAR-10 exception improve clarity and qualification. These gains are limited by reduced comparator coverage, missing uncertainty for ImageNet-200 accuracy, and insufficient timing details for the new speedup claims. Overall, v5 provides a modest quality improvement.
